description:
1052 tiles at 16x16 for the sea floor: a lit shell sand shelf, abyssal ooze, a coral reef, a kelp forest, a drowned city's pavement, talus, columnar vent rock and a trench that drops into black — with the wreck, the reef heads and the ruins lying on it. Commercial use permitted, in unlimited projects, with no attribution required; the one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the pack itself.

Importers for RPG Maker MZ, Tiled and Godot ship in the download, and each was run by the engine it targets and made to count what it built.

What is in the download

  • 611 of the 1052 tiles are transitions — 58% of the pack. 13 complete 47-mask autotile sets: every inner corner, outer corner, edge, junction and single. Completeness is checked mechanically on every build, because a 47-mask set missing three tiles is broken in your map and you find out while you are painting.
  • 8 materials × 4 variants on a value ladder laid out before any art existed, so a deep-water palette does not collapse into one blue-grey smear. The smallest gap on the ladder is 18.1 luma, measured from the shipped pixels.
  • 75 objects across 337 tiles — brain, fan and staghorn coral, tube sponges, anemones, a giant clam, standing kelp, a galleon's stern, an anchor, a cannon, a ship's wheel, chests, amphorae, columns and a statue from the drowned city, a whale skull and ribs, a diver's helmet and vent chimneys. They are 51 distinct silhouettes; the coral comes in 4 hues. Each ships transparent, and grounded on every surface it belongs to with the contact shadow drawn.
  • 10 animations, 72 frames: 8 caustic-light OVERLAYS you lay over your own sea floor, in two families meant to be stacked (broad patches of light, and the bright filaments where it folds), plus 2 animated objects — a swaying anemone and a vent plume.
  • A finished 36x26 sample map with 242 objects on it, as a PNG, as JSON naming every cell by tile id, and as a .tmx that opens in Tiled.
  • 80 4x4 proof renders, one per repeating tile, so you can look for the grid line yourself.
  • Every tile as a loose PNG and as packed sheets: 1216 files in total.

Two things to know before you buy

⚠️ The caustic overlays are opaque tiles. The pack's own proof requires alpha to be strictly 0 or 255, so there are no semi-transparent pixels anywhere in it. Put the caustics on their own layer and set that layer's opacity; every image on this page was made at 45%. Laid solid at 100% they replace the sea floor under them.

⚠️ The animation plays in Tiled and Godot, not in RPG Maker MZ. MZ animates tiles only through its A1 page, which holds animated water autotiles; this pack has none, so in MZ the animated tiles arrive as static frames on page D.

The importers were actually run

  • RPG Maker MZ — an A2 autotile sheet (the page MZ's own autotile brush paints) plus B/C/D/E object pages and a slot map. It composes correctly against MZ's own FLOOR_AUTOTILE_TABLE: 13 of 13 sets, 611 of 611 masked tiles, and 624 of 624 shapes came back byte-identical. The object pages carry every fill, every object and every animation frame; 339 of the 611 transitions also fit there as loose stamps, and all of them are on the A2 brush.
  • Tiled — one .tsx per group, all 17 opened and rendered by Tiled 1.12.2's own tmxrasterizer and compared pixel for pixel with the shipped sheets: 1,324 sheet cells, 0 differing. The sample map's .tmx renders 958,464 pixels identical to the shipped PNG.
  • Godot 4 — a .tres TileSet, loaded and verified in Godot 4.7.2: 17 atlas sources, 1052 of 1052 declared tiles built, 164 of 164 multi-cell footprints exact. Every sheet is referenced by a relative filename, so the folder loads from wherever you put it in a project.

What is proven, and what is not

The grid is exact, the palette is locked to 99 colours, the alpha is strictly binary with no anti-aliasing, every tile carries a declared role, and every autotile set is complete — exact checks, run on every build.

Seamlessness is not on that list. Every tile's wrap boundary is measured against its own interior, and every 4x4 repetition is rendered and reviewed; grid, palette and autotile completeness are machine-proven. The renders ship with the pack so you can judge them yourself.

It fits the rest of the series

The 16x16 Verdant packs are drawn at one cell size in one style, so this layer sits under the others.

  • Verdant 04 — Tidewater — the coast, river and marsh at the surface above it
  • Verdant 10 — Harbour — the docks and hulls a wreck would have sailed from
  • Verdant 11 — Vessel — the ship itself: deck, hull, hold and open sea

AI disclosure

Tagged as AI-assisted. Precisely: every tile is drawn by a procedural generator written for this series, and that generator's code was written with AI assistance — no diffusion model is anywhere in the tile pipeline. Every image on this page, the cover included, is composed from the pack's own tiles and sample map.
